newsitem.title: ITALY: San Paolo to offer 45 pct of bank for sale.
newsitem.headline: San Paolo to offer 45 pct of bank for sale.

text.p: Italian banking group San Paolo said it planned to offer a total stake of 45 percent in Istituto San Paolo di Torino bank through a private placement and a public sale offer (OPV).
A San Paolo statement said it planned to offer around 20 percent of the bank through a private placement to strategic and institutional investors.
It also planned to offer a further 25 percent on the domestic and international markets in a public sale offer.
Around 65 percent of Istituto San Paolo bank is currently held by the holding company San Paolo Bank Holding Spa, which in turn is 100 percent controlled by charity foundation Compagnia di San Paolo.
The privatisation plan aims to reduce the foundation's stake in the bank to around 20 to 25 percent by selling the controlling stake owned through the holding company.
"At the end of the project the bank will be a public company without controlling shareholders," it said.
The project envisaged two phases, with the first involving the creation of a stable group of shareholders through a private placement of 20 percent of the bank's capital.
The second was the public offer of the next 25 percent.
"At the end of the privatisation project, the foundation, directly, or through the holding, will have reduced its own stake to 20 to 25 percent," the statement said.
As far as that remnant stake was concerned there was also a plan for eventual "self-limit" on voting rights that still had to be worked out, it said.
Eventually functions of the holding would be assumed by the bank, with subsidiaries reporting directly to the bank, it said.
